questions.prompt: What is a network?
options: A single cable that carries electricity to a device
Two or more devices connected to share information
One computer running more than one program at once
A program that turns names into IP addresses

questions.prompt: In data communication, what is the medium?
options: The information that is being sent
The rules both sides agree to follow
The path the message travels on
The device that starts the talk

questions.prompt: In data communication, what is the protocol?
options: The agreed rules both sides follow
The cable that links the two sides
The picture or text being sent across
The device the message is meant for

questions.prompt: What lets other devices find one host among many?
What is a link?
options: The rules for sending a message
A program that waits for requests
A device that sends a message

questions.prompt: Which network covers one place, like a classroom or a ship?
What is the biggest WAN of all?
In a star topology, what is every device connected to?
In a star, one cable is cut. What is lost?
options: Only the device on that cable

questions.prompt: Which topology can be split in two by one broken backbone cable?
In which topology does data travel around a loop of neighbours?
How many links does a full mesh of 4 devices need?
What is the main downside of a mesh topology?
Which medium carries pulses of light through glass?
About how far can one run of twisted-pair Ethernet cable reach?
Why is wireless a poor choice while an enemy is jamming the area?
options: Wireless cannot carry any text at all
The air is shared and can be jammed
Wireless needs a cable to every device
Wireless only works over long distances

questions.prompt: What does a NIC do?
options: Splits one switch into virtual parts
Hands out IP addresses to new devices
Connects a device to the medium
Turns domain names into IP addresses

questions.prompt: What is a MAC address?
options: The unique hardware address of a NIC
The address a host uses to leave its network
The name of a server on the Internet
The number of hops to reach a host

questions.prompt: What is bandwidth?
options: How far a cable can reach without help
How many devices share the same link
How much data a link carries per second
How long one trip across the link takes

questions.prompt: What does ping's time tell you about a link?
How is a switch different from a hub?
options: A switch repeats every signal to every port
A switch connects different networks together
A switch sends traffic only to the right port
A switch has no ports, only wireless links

questions.prompt: What does a router connect?
What is a host's default gateway?
options: The switch port it is plugged into
The server that gives it a name
The router it uses to leave home
The cable that links it to a hub

questions.prompt: Two devices are plugged into the same switch but in different VLANs. Can they reach each other directly?
Why put the shield controller in its own VLAN?
options: To give it a faster wireless signal
To keep it apart from others, for security
To let it share a MAC address with others
To make its cable reach further than 100 meters

questions.prompt: In the client-server model, what does the server do?
Which server turns names into IP addresses?
Which server hands out IP addresses?
What does a hypervisor do?
options: Joins several computers into one big machine
Splits one computer into virtual machines
Checks every cable for a working signal
Turns a switch into a router for a short time

questions.prompt: Which cloud model gives you raw servers to manage yourself?
Online email you just log in and use is which cloud model?

options: The server has no route back to you
Your cable is longer than 100 meters
Your NIC has two MAC addresses
